payload.root_cause: In slugify(), the call .replace(/[\s-]+/, '-') on src/text.js:11 uses a regex WITHOUT the global (/g) flag. String.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the FIRST match, so after the first whitespace run is turned into a dash, all later gaps remain as spaces. For 'Hello Big  World!': lowercase+strip gives 'hello big  world', the first replace turns 'hello big' into 'hello-big', but the double space before 'world' is never replaced, yielding 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. The final trim regex (/^-+|-+$/g) correctly has /g, confirming the middle regex is the anomaly.

payload.rationale: The root cause is that the regex in the middle replace of slugify(), /[\s-]+/, is missing the global (/g) flag, so String.replace substitutes only the FIRST whitespace/dash run and later gaps remain as spaces. Adding /g makes every run of whitespace/dashes collapse to a single dash, so 'Hello Big  World!' becomes 'hello-big-world' and '  Already-slugged  title ' becomes 'already-slugged-title' (the surrounding trim and final /^-+|-+$/g cleanup already handle leading/trailing dashes). This matches the pattern of the adjacent regexes on lines 10 and 12, which both correctly use /g. The change is a one-character-class-flag edit with no other behavior impact.
